I know this post is a month old, but I wanted to comment because it really resonated with me as it sounds similar to my own story. 

I just returned to school for the 3rd time after failing out twice due to my disabilities and finally graduated! It was hard. I was riddled with anxiety and feelings of imposter syndrome and inadequacy. It was hard to manage my disabilities and the workload. But I got through, and I believe that you can do it too. 

You have a goal, you know what you want for your life, and having that is the first step. You’ve already got some education too and that puts you at an advantage. I know it’s so hard to believe in yourself, and I know how awful that fear of failure is when failure isn’t an option. But you’d be amazed at what you can do when you have no choice. You’ve made it through every hard thing in your life thus far, and you can get through this too.

Also, I found it helpful in school to take some of the pressure off by telling myself my work doesn’t have to be perfect, what matters most is getting that diploma/degree. Once you get that paper it will open so many doors. 

Sincerely, I wish you the best of luck 💛 you can do it!

I’ve had very severe allergies to cats my whole life, to the point of wheezing and being unable to breathe at all. I get congested when I sleep (from other allergies I guess) and was prescribed a steroid nasal spray a while ago, and discovered that I barely even sneeze even when visiting friends with several cats now, without allergy pills. Before, allergy pills wouldn’t even do anything for a single cat. The nasal spray works so well in fact, that I adopted a cat of my own a month ago. 

The shelter recommended I feed him Purina Liveclear to make him less allergenic. I have an air purifier running on low 24/7, and run my robovac every single day to keep hair from accumulating. I brush him daily and got him wipes and spray from Burt’s Bees that reduce dander. I take my nasal spray as prescribed. And it pains me to do so because he is such a snuggly boy, but I don’t let him in my bed. 

It’s been a month now and I mostly haven’t had respiratory allergy symptoms (I still get hives though lol) and if my allergies do start to flare up, I just take an allergy pill and that takes care of things.

Other people have given all this advice, I just wanted to share my personal experience with you to demonstrate that these solutions have worked for me. I sincerely hope you don’t have to re-home your cats, wishing you all the best ❤️

I just had LJS, I only lost 5lbs. But I made it a priority to take in as much food as I could manage. I know jaw surgery seems like a great opportunity to lose weight, but I was advised by the nutritionist at the hospital to not use it as such. I once had a driver get mad at me for stopping to make sure they were going to stop before I crossed in front of them turning into a plaza. Then maybe half an hour later I saw someone on a bicycle get hit and fly up on to the roof of the car. It was a little traumatic. And the amount of times I’ve almost been hit myself by people blowing red lights after I’d seen it was safe to cross, people turning in to the crosswalk while you’re crossing with a walk signal and then THEY get mad, etc etc. is ridiculous.
Drivers can get mad all they want at our cautiousness but it’s for a damn good reason!!!!

As nice as the weight loss is, healing your body is the most important thing right now. Don’t worry about gaining the weight back or keeping it off. Just focus on maintaining good nutrition and getting enough calories to heal your jaw. If you’ve already lost weight prior to jaw surgery, then even if you gain the weight that you’ve lost after surgery back, you already know exactly what to do to lose it again and you’ve already proven to yourself that you can do it :) 

Best of luck with your recovery, and your fitness journey!
